questions.prompt: On Gemini Omni Flash, how do you ask for a video that loops from one image?

options.text: Use the same image as the first and the last frame
options.explanation: Right. The Gemini API docs say the same image as first and last frame creates a video that loops.

options.text: Use the image as a reference, not as a frame
options.explanation: A reference guides the look. It does not tie the end of the clip back to its start.

options.text: Ask for a 10-second clip with no image at all
options.explanation: Length does not make a loop, and without the image the approved look is lost.

questions.prompt: Luma rejects video.loop together with which setting?

options.explanation: start_frame works with loop. That is how you loop from an approved still.
Right. The Luma docs say keyframes is mutually exclusive with start_frame, end_frame and loop.
5 seconds is the default, and loop needs it: loop is rejected with 10s.

questions.prompt: The end card must show the client's logo exactly. What is the safest plan?

options.text: Animate around the logo, or add the real logo file in your editor
options.explanation: Right. Exact things are finished by hand (Prompt Forest, chapter 4). Keep the logo still or add it after (our advice).

options.text: Let the model redraw the logo, and check only the first frame
options.explanation: Letters can change in the middle of a clip. Every frame needs a check.

options.text: Ask the model to spin the logo fast, so small errors are hidden
options.explanation: Fast motion does not stop a frame-by-frame check from finding bent letters.
